description: Expected security findings for each blind test file. Use this to score the CyberLLM pipeline's detection accuracy.

expected_findings.title: SQL injection via string concatenation
expected_findings.detail: cursor.execute uses %-formatting to interpolate user-supplied 'vin' directly into SQL string

expected_findings.title: Raw SQL with f-string interpolation
expected_findings.detail: f-string builds SQL with unsanitized 'owner_name' and 'status' parameters

expected_findings.title: Raw SQL with f-string interpolation
expected_findings.detail: f-string builds DELETE query with unsanitized 'record_id' — allows arbitrary deletion or SQL injection

expected_findings.title: Path traversal
expected_findings.detail: User-controlled 'filename' from request.args concatenated to base path without sanitization; attacker uses ../../etc/passwd

expected_findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
expected_findings.detail: User-supplied URL passed directly to urlopen without allow-list or schema/host validation

expected_findings.title: Path traversal
expected_findings.detail: User-controlled 'file' parameter from request.args used in f-string path to open(); allows directory traversal

expected_findings.title: Hard-coded secret
expected_findings.detail: API key 'sk_prod_4f8a9c2b1d6e3f7a0b5c8d2e1a9f4c6b' embedded directly in source code

expected_findings.title: Hard-coded credential in connection string
expected_findings.detail: PostgreSQL connection string contains username:password in plaintext

expected_findings.title: Hard-coded secret
expected_findings.detail: JWT access token embedded in source code

expected_findings.title: Weak hash for credentials
expected_findings.detail: hashlib.md5 used for password hashing — trivially crackable, no salt

expected_findings.title: Non-cryptographic randomness for security
expected_findings.detail: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) used for session tokens — state is predictable

expected_findings.title: Non-cryptographic randomness for security
expected_findings.detail: random.randint for OTP generation — attacker can predict next values

expected_findings.title: Unsafe deserialization (pickle)
expected_findings.detail: pickle.loads on untrusted input — attacker crafts payload to execute arbitrary code during deserialization

expected_findings.title: Unsafe deserialization (yaml.load)
expected_findings.detail: yaml.load with yaml.Loader allows !!python/object tags to instantiate arbitrary classes

expected_findings.title: Unsafe deserialization (eval)
expected_findings.detail: eval() on base64-decoded user input — arbitrary code execution

expected_findings.title: eval() of decoded payload
expected_findings.detail: eval(base64.b64decode(...)) pattern — classic RCE vector

expected_findings.title: Command injection sink
expected_findings.detail: subprocess.check_output with shell=True and user-controlled f-string command

expected_findings.title: Unsafe deserialization (eval)
expected_findings.detail: eval() on user-supplied formula string — even with restricted builtins, bypass is trivial

expected_findings.title: JWT algorithm 'none' accepted
expected_findings.detail: algorithms list includes 'none' — attacker removes signature and forges any token payload

expected_findings.title: Authorization trusts client-supplied role header
expected_findings.detail: Server reads role from X-User-Role header set by client — attacker sends 'admin' to bypass authorization

expected_findings.title: IDOR — ownership check missing
expected_findings.detail: Any authenticated user can query any vehicle_id without ownership verification

expected_findings.title: Sensitive endpoint without authentication
expected_findings.detail: /debug/dump-db exposes entire database with no auth check at all

expected_findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
expected_findings.detail: verify=False disables certificate validation — enables MITM attacks

expected_findings.title: Unsafe C string operation (strcpy)
expected_findings.detail: strcpy into fixed-size buffer with no bounds check — stack buffer overflow

expected_findings.title: Unsafe C string operation (sprintf)
expected_findings.detail: sprintf into fixed-size buffer — overlong vin causes overflow

expected_findings.title: Format-string vulnerability
expected_findings.detail: printf(user_msg) without format specifier — attacker injects %x/%n to read/write memory

expected_findings.title: Unsafe C string operation (gets)
expected_findings.detail: gets() has no bounds checking — can never be used safely, deprecated in C11

expected_findings.title: Non-constant-time secret comparison
expected_findings.detail: strcmp for token comparison leaks length via timing side-channel

expected_findings.title: Format-string vulnerability
expected_findings.detail: sprintf(log_buf, error_from_network) — user-controlled format string

07_vehicle_utils.py.note: NEGATIVE CONTROL — this file is intentionally clean. All operations (hashing, subprocess, SQL, file I/O, HTTP) are done correctly. Any finding reported here is a FALSE POSITIVE.
